To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a single residue, Asp575, is required for K+ dependence of Na+/Ca2+/K+ transport in NCKX2 and that this residue is conserved in NCKX1 and NCKX3–5 but replaced by asparagine in the three NCx isoforms, which are K+-independent.
substitution of Asp575 by asparagine or by cysteine in NCKX2 rendered the transporter K+-independent, while replacement of the same residue by glutamate rendered the transporter nonfunctional.
a single amino acid substitution in the NCKXXP motif renders NCKX2 independent of K+ and results in a K+-independent Ca2+ extruder.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of residues in NCKX2 that are important for the transport of K+ and Ca2+, and the results provide new insight into the molecular mechanism of the NCKX proteins.

the molecular mechanism underlying the K+-dependent Na+-Ca2+ exchange and has identified a single residue, Asp575, that is critical for K+ transport by NCKX2 and may be a key component of the mechanism of K+ transport in the NCKx family.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a single charge in the Na+/Ca2+/K+ exchanger, Asp575, is responsible for the dependence on K+ of the exchanger.
Asp575 is the key determinant of K+ dependence of Ca2+ extruding NCKXs.
Asp575 in NCKX2 and NCKX1 plays a critical role in the coupling of the Na+ and K+ gradients, and that this coupling is essential for the function of the Na+/Ca2+:K+ exchanger.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a single residue in the NCKx proteins, Asp575, is the determinant of K+ dependence of Ca2+ extruding transport activity.
Asp575 is the key residue for the K+-dependent transport function of NCKX2.
a single residue, Asp575 in NCKX2, determines whether the exchanger will be K+ dependent or independent.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the K+-dependence of NCKX is not a property of a large number of residues, as is the case for the K+-dependent Na+,K+-ATPase, but rather is a property of a single residue, Asp575.
a single residue, located in transmembrane helix 9 of the transporter, determines the K+ dependence or independence of the transporter.
the Asp575 residue in NCKX2 plays a critical role in the K+ dependence and is likely to be involved in the K+ binding site.
